【答案（自然语言）】Summed social capital — defined by project convention as the sum of the standardized (Z) time series for Copper & Gold, Amber, and Monument Count (interpolated series, no re-standardization) — peaked in the 14th century BCE (≈1400–1301 BCE; calBP 3350–3251), within a clearly Late-Bronze-Age peak plateau spanning the 12th–14th centuries BCE (century means 4.24 / 3.93 / 3.62 Z, all >2.3 Z above any other period; 50/100/150-year smoothed curves all peak in the 14th c. BCE; on the non-interpolated century knots the 13th and 14th centuries tie exactly at 4.238). The components that rose with the summed curve were Copper/Gold (peak 12th c. BCE, +3.11 Z above the earliest baseline, r=0.68 with the sum, rising sustainedly from the 15th c. BCE onward) and Monument Count (peaked much earlier at 27th c. BCE but climbed steadily from the 18th c. BCE, +2.48 Z at the peak, r=0.69); together they drive the peak (leave-one-out: dropping Copper/Gold moves the maximum to the 27th c. BCE, dropping Amber or Monument Count does not; variance shares 0.40/0.39/0.21). Amber did NOT follow as a driver: its own maximum is in the 31st c. BCE (early Neolithic), it only recovered from a 19th–20th c. BCE trough (−1.07 to −0.01 Z) and remained 1.2 Z below the early baseline (r=0.36). Monument Size (assigned by convention to economic capital, not summed) moved synchronously (peak 15th c. BCE). Caveats: Z-additivity, member composition (MonumentSize excluded), and the century rule floor((−CE−1)/100)+1 are conventions/assumptions; adding MonumentSize would tilt the peak toward the 15th c. BCE; pollen context (Belau, reference only) shows moderate openness around the peak, with no pollen-file coverage for −701…−500.

【Workflow】Master table: time_series_data.csv (annual, CE=−BCE, identical to capital.csv Z values on all 37 shared knots, max|diff|=0); soc = CopperGold_inter + Amber_inter + MonumentCount_inter; century = floor((−CE−1)/100)+1; peak judged by century means, robustness via raw-knot series, 50/100/150y centered rolling means, leave-one-out, variance decomposition, pairwise correlations, early-baseline (41–37 cBCE) rise amplitudes, and a sensitivity adding capital.csv's exclusive 4300/4200 BCE rows (soc=−2.594; peak unchanged).

payload.hypothesis: Summed social capital (Z-standardized Copper&Gold + Amber + Monument Count, interpolated series) peaked in the 14th century BCE (~1400-1301 BCE; calBP 3350-3251), on a Late Bronze Age peak plateau (12th-14th c. BCE) confirmed by 50/100/150-year smoothing and by non-interpolated century knots (13th/14th c. tie at 4.238 Z). The components that rose together with the summed curve were Copper/Gold (peak 12th c. BCE, +3.11 Z above the earliest 5-century baseline, r=0.68 with the sum) and Monument Count (sustained rise from the 18th c. BCE, +2.48 Z at the peak, r=0.69); these two jointly drive the peak (leave-one-out: removing Copper/Gold shifts the maximum to the 27th c. BCE; variance shares 0.40/0.39/0.21). Amber did not drive the peak - its maximum lies in the 31st c. BCE and it merely recovered from a 19th-20th c. BCE trough (r=0.36). Monument Size, classified by convention as economic capital, was synchronous (peak 15th c. BCE). Conventions/assumptions: Z additivity, capital-category membership, and century boundaries floor((-CE-1)/100)+1; adding MonumentSize would tilt the peak toward the 15th c. BCE. Background pollen openness (Belau) was moderate near the peak; pollen lacks coverage for -701...-500 BCE.
payload.workflow: 1) Verified 12 column pairs identical between capital.csv and time_series_data.csv on 37 shared century knots (max|diff|=0) and that *_inter columns are linear interpolations (np.interp reconstruction, diff ~1e-16); adopted time_series_data.csv as master (annual, CE= negative BCE, calBP=1950-CE). 2) soc = CopperGold_inter + Amber_inter + MonumentCount_inter (no re-standardization; each Z column mean~0/std~1 at knots). 3) Century assignment: floor((-CE-1)/100)+1. 4) Peak judged by century means; robustness: raw-knot parallel series, centered 50/100/150-year rolling means, top-5 century gaps, leave-one-out component removal, variance decomposition cov(comp,soc)/var(soc). 5) Component trends: peak century, sustained rise interval, early baseline (41-37 cBCE) rise amplitude, pairwise and sum correlations. 6) Pollen_inter_100 / pollen_grate_100 reported as non-decision background with explicit coverage gap (-701...-500 forward-filled). 7) Sensitivity merging capital.csv-exclusive 4300/4200 BCE rows (soc=-2.594; peak unchanged). Script: analysis/final_analysis.py; outputs: analysis/output_report.txt, analysis/century_table.csv.
